title: Evidence-first claim ledger
description: Machine-readable claim ledger. Every material claim carries a mechanism, evidence, scope, and status. The checkable subset of this schema is enforced by tools/claim_lint.py (checks L1-L4); check L5 scans prose documents for unqualified absolutes.

project.description: Name of the project the ledger describes.

generated.description: Date the ledger was last regenerated by hand or tooling.

retired.description: Tombstones for claims removed from `claims` (V2-05). tools/status_diff.py errors when a base claim disappears without one; tools/claim_lint.py rejects a tombstone with no reason and one that names an active claim. Append-only: dropping a tombstone later is an error in the diff.

status.description: The strongest honest label the evidence supports. proven: machine-checked proof with declared assumptions. model-checked: exhaustive or bounded exploration, state the bound. tested: executed tests that attempt the violation. static-refinement: analysis with tool and triage. reviewed: human review only. open: claim exists, evidence does not.

artifact.description: Path to the evidence artifact relative to the project root (or a URL). Lint check L2 verifies existence.

command.description: Command that reproduces the result. Required alongside artifact for kind=test.

commit.description: Commit the evidence was produced at. Lint check L2 verifies resolvability.

date.description: When the evidence was produced. Lint check L2 flags stale evidence.

tests.description: Test IDs that attempt the violation. Required when kind=test. Lint check L3 verifies each ID exists in the suite.

run_record.description: Machine-checkable record of the executed run (V2-01). Optional, but a kind=test record without one gets an L2 warning; with one, L2 checks the log and artifact hashes, the exit code, and that every cited test appears in the log.

tool_output.description: The model checker's or prover's own run (V2-10). A status of model-checked or proven needs one; an artifact alone proves only that a model exists. L2 checks the output hash and the exit code, L4 rejects a model-checked or proven claim without a tool_output.

scope.description: Where the claim applies and what is outside the trust boundary.

actors_excluded.description: Privileged actors outside the threat model: superuser, DBA, deployment admin, and so on.

claim.description: Falsifiable statement. 'The system is secure' is not a claim; 'role Y cannot write T through any supported entry point' is.

mechanism.description: What in the system is supposed to make the claim true.

limitations.description: Known limits and residual risk, stated next to the claim. Required when status is open.

last_verified.description: When the evidence was last rerun. Stale evidence is a finding, not a formality.
